name: Platonism
summary: Platonism holds that reality's true objects are unchanging Forms, crowned by the Form of the Good, knowable by reason rather than the senses. Its political implications, as scholars draw them from the Republic and Laws, are that justice means each part of the city and soul doing its proper task, that those who know the good should rule, and that education and law should aim at the virtue of citizens. It is hostile to democracy as rule by the unlearned and favours regulation of wealth and culture.
scope: Platonism as a philosophy, with political implications drawn from Plato's Republic and Laws as presented by the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy. Neoplatonism, modern Platonism about abstract objects, and Plato's other dialogues are not the basis. Many answers on modern policy questions are inferences and marked low confidence.

sources.title: Plato's Laws
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Mixed constitution, land allotments and wealth limits, penalties aimed at reform, impiety laws, persuasive preludes, exclusion of crafts.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Republic III, where medicine is a state concern but limited to those fit to live useful lives, so adherents would not endorse a modern universal entitlement outright.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the city's concern to limit extremes of wealth and poverty; wage-setting itself never arises.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the rulers' direction of the producing class and the Laws' tight limits on trade and wealth.

public-ownership.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a city where guardians own nothing but producers keep private property, so ownership of industry is not decisive.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' limits on the gap between rich and poor.

unions-good.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the principle that each person does one task and classes stay in harmony, which leaves no room for organized sectional bargaining.

property-fundamental.rationale: Guardians hold no private property and the Laws moderate wealth and keep land in fixed allotments, so property is subordinate to the city's good.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' regulation of crafts, trade and wealth in the interest of virtue.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the concern that extreme poverty and wealth corrupt the city; but no welfare policy is discussed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the principle of specialization, under which producers produce and rulers govern.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from rulers who oversee citizens' conduct for the good of the city.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' regulation of pleasures such as wine as training in self-control.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Republic's censorship of speech and stories that harm civic character.

strong-leader.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Republic's ideal of a wise ruler unconstrained by faction, though the Laws prefers rule of law.

state-harmful.rationale: The city is where justice is achieved and the Republic's whole project is to design the best state, so a stateless life is rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a city whose guardians and citizens are armed under public authority; private gun ownership is not addressed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the strong auxiliary class that defends the city, whose authority is kept in check by education.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the regulation of sexual life by the city in the Republic and Laws.

decide-locally.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the small city-state setting, in which rulers decide for the whole unit; the national-versus-local question does not arise.

rehabilitation.rationale: The Laws says penalties aim to make offenders more virtuous or less vicious, with deterrence as a further aim.

traditional-family.rationale: The Republic abolishes private families among guardians, though the Laws keeps households, so adherents are not defenders of the traditional family as society's foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' regulation of sexual conduct to serve the city's virtue; marriage is a public institution.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the state's control of reproduction among the guardians; adherents are not clearly on either side of the modern question.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Laws requires belief in gods who care for humans and punishes impiety, and the Republic makes piety part of justice.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from principles of justice as desert; the question is anachronistic.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The Republic argues that the difference between the sexes is irrelevant to ruling, which treats role differences as largely a matter of training.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Republic's state-controlled education and the Laws' wariness of novelty.

gradual-change.rationale: The Laws forbids varying children's games so as not to breed a taste for institutional change, though the Republic itself proposes a radical founding.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' closed, tightly regulated citizen body.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the polis as the unit of justice.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' limits on trade and the ideal of a self-sufficient city.

nation-first.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a polis-centred ethic, set against the Republic's call for Greeks to treat other Greeks differently from outsiders.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no settled view on intervention for rights.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a bounded city with defined citizenship.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; the simple city of the Republic is contrasted with a luxurious one that breeds war, but environment is not discussed.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from rule by knowledge: if experts identify a grave threat, rulers should act decisively.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the view that human problems are solved by wisdom about the good, not by craft or technique.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

revolution-justified.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Republic's preference for rule by the wise and its distrust of faction.

experts-over-public.rationale: Central: cities will not be free of evils until philosophers rule, since only those who know the good should govern.

central-planning.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from rulers directing production, set against the producers' own economic life.

socialized-markets.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

land-value-tax.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' caps on wealth and fixed allotments.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the principle that everyone performs a function in the city.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' control of trade for the sake of self-sufficiency.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from rulers directing the economy toward the city's good.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' equal land allotments and limits on wealth.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a city where producers keep property and guardians receive support from them.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from classes living in harmony under the rulers' guidance.

one-party-rule.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a ruling guardian class guided by knowledge of the good; scholars note the parallel, but it is not a party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The ideal ruler is a philosopher-king, and the Laws treats moderate monarchy as one good element of a constitution.

democracy-best.rationale: The Republic presents democracy as a degenerate regime on the road to tyranny, and the Laws prefers a mixture of monarchy and democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Rule by the unlearned many is the defect of democracy; decisions belong to those with knowledge.

workers-councils.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the rejection of rule by producers.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the value placed on the unity of the city.

natural-rulers.rationale: Central: rulers are chosen for the philosophical nature suited to knowing the good, as against the many.

political-violence-never.rationale: Plato accepts war and force in the city; no pacifist reading is available.

war-builds-character.rationale: Adherents are split: the Republic trains martial guardians, while the Laws criticizes organizing the city around war.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Laws puts religion under law, with impiety a crime, and the Republic supervises stories about the gods.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Platonism has no scripture; laws are to rest on reason and the lawgiver's knowledge, with religion as support.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defense is the duty of the guardian class and justice is a public function of the city.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the guardians' strength balanced by a warning that luxury leads to war.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The city's three classes are meant to live in harmony, and decline comes from appetite's corruption, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Justice is each doing the task suited to them, with unequal roles; guardians are communal but the classes differ.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

civilizational-union.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Republic answers Thrasymachus by arguing that justice, not self-advantage, is the real good, and rulers gain nothing for themselves.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Justice means each part performing its function for the whole, and the city's unity outranks individual claims.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed in the political sources used.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' fixed-size city.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' wariness of innovation and stress on stability.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a view that excellence comes through education and virtue.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from rule by wise persons rather than mechanical procedure.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from rulers' oversight of the city.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Republic narrates decline from an ideal but does not call for restoration of a past order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from policy being guided by knowledge of the Good rather than by trial and outcomes.

direct-action.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the distrust of faction and rule by the many.

means-match-ends.rationale: Mixed: justice in the soul and city are parallel, yet the Republic allows a state 'noble lie'.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The Republic's simple city is an agricultural community of specialists, not foragers.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The principle of specialization, each doing the one task they are best suited for, underlies justice in the city.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from justice as each performing their own function and receiving accordingly.

production-for-use.rationale: Split between the simple city that produces for needs and the luxurious city that the Republic criticizes without banning.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a city in which producers are a dependent but legitimate class.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule by the producing class over others contradicts rule by the wise.

collective-farming.rationale: The Laws divides land into household allotments and rejects farming in common.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anachronistic, though the Republic does trace war to the pursuit of luxury and excess.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a state whose legitimacy and claims on citizens' resources are taken for granted.

harm-principle.rationale: The city is to make citizens virtuous, using censorship and laws against impiety, not merely to prevent harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a city whose unity is placed above individual claims.

conscription.rationale: Defense is a duty of the guardians, and the Laws expects citizens to take part in defense.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Neither exit nor voting are checks Platonists favour; the check is the rulers' knowledge and law.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a city oriented to justice and virtue rather than customers and profit.

positive-liberty.rationale: Freedom is rational self-rule, with Laws calling obedience to law a kind of freedom; material means are not discussed.

media-academia-power.rationale: A factual claim about modern institutions; Platonists stress educators' influence but no stance is documented.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial groups are not discussed; nature is held to shape who is fit to rule, but not by race.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from rule by the wise, not by representatives of interests.

total-state.rationale: The ideal city directs education, culture, and economic roles under the rulers, though not as a modern total state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Republic traces war to expanding beyond needs through luxury.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on knowledge and law, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from producers as a free but subordinate class.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Platonism holds that knowledge of unchanging Forms is real and reached through reason, not power.

universal-morality.rationale: Central: the Form of the Good and the virtues are objective and known by reason.

single-common-good.rationale: The city aims at one good, justice, determined by those who know it, and not at balancing interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

revive-national-language.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the rejection of rule by the unlearned many.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is a core state function in both the Republic and the Laws, so parental choice of school is not favoured.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Republic's view that wealth corrupts regimes and political order is shaped by virtue.

rule-by-example.rationale: Split: rulers' virtue matters, but the Laws is a full law code with preludes plus penalties.

national-self-determination.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

force-without-un.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Knowledge comes through reason and dialectic, though the philosophy also holds a place for myth and piety.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' sharp line between citizens and resident foreigners.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the principle that everyone performs their own function in the city.

class-collaboration.rationale: Justice in the city is each class doing its own work in harmony, with no struggle between classes.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Plato distrusts novelty and prizes education, though he also censors inherited poetry.

dominated-front.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

workers-nation.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Republic argues that women can be educated and rule as guardians, so law should not fix separate public roles.

ban-interest.rationale: The Laws is commonly said to forbid lending at interest; this audit did not open the passage.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: No racial classification in the political works; the city is divided by natural fitness.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Republic refutes the claim that rule serves the stronger; true rulers aim at the good of the ruled.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' emphasis on a shared way of life.

elite-replacement.rationale: A modern conspiracy claim with no basis in the sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' mixed system of election and lot, not party shares.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a city seeking virtue within its own borders.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Republic treats female inequality as a matter of education, but the claim is not addressed.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Republic stresses that existing regimes are corrupted by appetite and that philosophers are rare.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Regulation of guardian reproduction by the city is part of the Republic; this audit did not read the specific passage.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state must foster virtue through education and law, not just protect property and justice.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The city is divided into classes by natural aptitude, though women can qualify equally for guardianship.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' penalties for impiety and state religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Education in piety and about the gods is part of the city's teaching.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority rests on knowledge, though the Laws uses persuasion through preludes.

trade-surplus.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

population-transfer.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Honour- and gain-seeking are marks of defective regimes, not engines of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the distrust of faction and defense of the constitution.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The city uses coercion in law and punishment, so the principle is rejected.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Freedom is obedience to law and reason, but non-domination is not discussed.

separated-powers.rationale: The Laws' mixed constitution divides offices between elective and lot-based elements.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a guardian class that leads others who lack knowledge.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from a city organized around the good of the whole, not any one class.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from limits on property in the Laws and Republic.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from class harmony and distrust of faction.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the view that poverty and wealth are controlled by institutions.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the importance placed on civic unity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Split: the Republic dismisses democratic methods, while the Laws fills some offices by lot.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the rulers' broad authority.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' controlled economy.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Republic's state censorship of stories and poetry.

party-commands-army.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Laws' limits on foreigners.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Guardians own nothing and rulers gain nothing for themselves, so office is service.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the guardians' unity of purpose.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the polis as the unit of rule.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Plato never addressed this question, and nothing in his political works lets it be inferred, so adherents are treated as neutral.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule belongs to philosophers, not priests, though religion is supported by law.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the duty of citizens to defend their city.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The Republic subjects poets and nursery tales to state censorship so that guardians grow up virtuous.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: philosopher rulers rule while fit, but the Laws sets short offices with scrutiny, and the statement is about elected presidents, so it is neutral.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred: Plato distrusts rule by the unlearned and the Laws checks officials by audit boards, not by voters removing them.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed directly; the ideal city is small and self-sufficient and its guardians defend it, but alliances and overseas troops are not discussed (inferred).

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred from the Laws, where equal land allotments are kept in each household and not sold, so families hold their own homes rather than renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Republic gives defence to a specialised guardian class trained for it, in line with its principle that each does one task.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred from the Laws, which places the city away from the sea and commerce so that trade does not corrupt citizens.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources used; inferred from the Republic that adherents would have no settled view on reunifying divided peoples.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Philosophers who know the good are the proper rulers, so adherents reject the idea that the educated are out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred: belief in objective Forms and a Form of the Good implies that ways of life can be better or worse, so cultures are not simply different.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred: the Laws punishes grave offences severely, with penalties aimed at reform and removal of the incurable.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: the Republic gives guardian women the same education as men and puts education under the state, so adherents would accept state-taught sex and sex equality.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: the Laws argues for divine order and punishes impiety, so adherents would accept teaching design alongside materialist accounts.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The Republic subjects poetry, tales and art to state censorship to protect moral character, so restricting pornography follows.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred: the Laws fixes a set number of allotted households passed down in families, so citizenship by descent fits.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred: the ideal city keeps one shared education and civic culture, so minority-language support is not part of the picture.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Laws enforces state religion through impiety laws, so adherents would not exempt groups from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The ideal city controls education, stories and art to produce unity and virtue, so social pressure to conform is endorsed rather than resisted.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; the Laws bars interest-lending yet Plato fears upheaval from debt abolition, so inference leaves it split.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Plato ties justice to the city's economic order, but the question of colonial-style independence is anachronistic; inferred as split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Plato has a wise lawgiver or founding commission design the constitution, not a mass elected body; inferred from the Laws' founding scenario.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Plato accepts heavy restriction but for virtue, not economic growth, which he distrusts as a goal; inferred from the Republic and Laws.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Plato's duties run to fellow citizens of the city; global aid is anachronistic and inferred as split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Plato prizes the self-sufficient, self-defending city, from which independent defence is inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Plato is hostile to rule by the unlearned masses and would rather the knowers rule, so popular election of the leader is disfavoured.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Expert, virtue-minded guardians regulating money insulated from popular pressure fits Platonic principles; inferred, not stated.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed; no clear Platonic principle on territorial compromise.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: In the Republic the guardians hold no property and the Laws treat allotments as the city's, so property is subordinate to the common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anachronistic and not a Platonic question; no basis for a side.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; the ancient city has no concept of environmental risk, so it is neutral.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; the Republic treats wars among Greeks as civil strife and the Laws gives no alliance rule, so adherents have no clear position.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed directly; the Republic limits the city's size but gives no view on annexation under law.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Laws puts religion under the city's law, with state officials supervising shrines and forbidding private cults, so religious bodies serve the polis.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Republic and Laws treat faction as the greatest evil for a city and place rulers above class interest, so a unifying figure above parties fits.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the Republic's view that unity is the greatest good of a city and division its greatest evil.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from the Laws, which has one code of law and one educational system for the whole city rather than separate systems within it.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Republic's rulers are chosen for knowledge, not descent, and the founding myth gives citizens metal-souls rather than divine lineage; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Laws divides citizens into property classes whose obligations differ, which is inferred to oppose a single uniform rate.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Republic holds that natures differ at birth (the myth of metals) even though education shapes them; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Laws calls rulers servants of the law and says a city whose law is subject to a ruler is near ruin, though the Republic lets philosopher-rulers act on knowledge.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from the Republic's small city with limited territory and wealth, which is opposed to open-ended expansion.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The Laws recommends a constitution that blends monarchic and democratic elements, as the SEP describes.

leader-cult.rationale: The Republic condemns flattery of rulers and the tyrant's hunger for adulation, though it honours its best guardians; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; the Republic abolishes private family life for the guardians and the Laws leaves families to the state, so no custody presumption is stated.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred from the Republic's view that faction is the disease of a city and that justice means each class doing its own task.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Laws allots equal land lots to citizens and limits wealth to keep the city united.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; the Laws treat citizenship as a fixed number of households, but nothing says about returning refugees.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from the Republic's ideal of a small city of limited size, which gives no ground for claims over distant co-nationals.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Laws prescribe penalties up to death for persistent impiety and the state guards belief, so punishing abandonment of civic religion fits.

women-must-cover.rationale: In Republic V the women guardians train unclothed with the men, so a covering law is inferred to be against his scheme.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from the Laws, which keep a local coinage for citizens and restrict wealth-getting through money.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Republic V treats Greeks as kin by nature who should regard wars among them as civil strife; inferred as favouring unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Republic puts education under state control to shape all citizens alike, leaving little room for separate minority schools.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; inferred only from his focus on fixed citizen households, which does not settle the question.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Republic holds that knowledge of the Good and the rule of reason, not material arrangements, should order the city.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from the Laws' regulation of trade and its limits on wealth, which would favour curbing concentrations of economic power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; the Laws regulate debt and wealth, but nothing speaks to rescuing failing firms.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Laws make law, not the will of the many, supreme and Plato is hostile to rule by majority.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: In Republic V women guardians receive the same education and may rule, so near equal representation fits his scheme.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Laws place the city away from the sea and restrict trade and foreign contact to keep it self-sufficient.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; the Laws regulate trade but have no notion of binding international agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Republic has guardians own no property and be spurred by honour and the love of the good rather than reward.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from the Republic's view that change comes from philosopher rulers and education, and that faction is a disease.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Republic selects guardians by nature, not birth, and allows children to move between classes.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Plato's education aims at knowledge of the Good, not national history, and the Republic never sets out a history curriculum; adherents have no clear view.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Republic has those who know the good rule the less wise for their benefit, which supports tutelage in principle, though the passage concerns classes in a city, not peoples.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Republic's education and the noble lie train guardians to love and defend the city, so teaching civic loyalty is stated as a goal; flag and anthem are not named.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; the Republic selects rulers by nature and training, which is neither for nor against racial preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: The Laws gives the state strict control of wealth and the currency, so public control over money creation is inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalism and its crises are anachronistic and not addressed.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The Republic traces war to the city's pursuit of luxury and expansion, and the Laws city is meant to be modest, so projecting influence abroad is inferred to be disfavoured.

delink-world-market.rationale: The Laws city is meant to be self-sufficient with limited trade and foreign contact, so inward economic focus is inferred; poor versus rich countries is not addressed.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-era thesis not addressed by Plato; no position can be inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The state in the Republic and Laws regulates economic and social life to serve virtue, so an unrestricted private right to discriminate is inferred to be rejected.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Both works put the wise or the law above individual claims, and rights against the state are an anachronistic idea, so an entrenched bill of rights is inferred to be disfavoured.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Plato does not discuss colonial treaties; nothing in his political writings bears on them.

elective-rulers.rationale: In the Republic rulers are chosen by education and proven wisdom, not by popular election, and election by the many is condemned; the Laws does use elections for some offices.

minority-veto.rationale: Wise rule binds all citizens, and the Republic gives no consent-based veto to those who disagree.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Laws holds rulers to be servants of the law and condemns tyranny; the right of subjects to resist is inferred from that.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Republic distrusts mass assemblies and the Laws prefers a mixed constitution with a nocturnal council, so legislative supremacy of an assembly is not endorsed.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Plato does not address animal suffering in his political works; the question is inferred and unsettled.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The city in the Republic eats meat and uses animals; humane treatment is inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Guardians must rule for the good of the ruled, and philosophers are compelled to return to the cave; the wealthy specifically are not addressed, so this is inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The philosopher prefers contemplation but is obliged in the ideal city to return and rule, though he stands aside in corrupt cities.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The Republic censors poetry and music and the Laws attacks theatrocracy because culture shapes citizens' character; Plato wants it to uphold the city's order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The noble lie and the guardians' education secure consent to the class order through culture; this is inferred from those passages.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The question is anachronistic and Plato does not discuss world economies; the Laws only limits trade and wealth.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Laws reserves offices and land for citizens and restricts resident foreigners; inferred from Magnesia's rules.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist parties are outside Plato's world; no inference is possible.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The Laws urges a city to be largely self-sufficient and to limit foreign trade and contact; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The Laws limits territory to what the city can support and sets peace as the aim of war, so claims to lost land are not encouraged; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Rule belongs to those with wisdom, not those with ancestry, though the Republic's myth of earth-born citizens is inferred to support citizens of the land; the weight is toward merit.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; Plato's regime is later labelled authoritarian but the constitutional value of anti-fascism does not apply.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; Plato does not address modern totalitarianism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Plato does not address the American Civil War.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Plato regulates public honours and art by their effect on virtue, with no clear rule for condemned figures; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Guardians are selected and educated by aptitude regardless of sex, with no special programmes for either; inferred from Republic Book V.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The Republic abolishes the private household for the guardians, and the Laws does not address symmetry of domestic violence; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The Laws says a constitution should be fitted to a people's character, land and climate; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The guardian class of auxiliaries defends and keeps order in the Republic, but under the rule of philosophers.

paid-care-work.rationale: The Republic abolishes the family for guardians and has care provided communally, so paying domestic work is outside its frame; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the Republic and Laws, where honouring parents is a duty of law and piety; the Laws penalises neglect of parents.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Republic places rule in philosopher-guardians selected by long education and testing of ability, not by election, wealth or birth.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the Laws' concern to protect the city's land and wealth from outside influence and to limit foreign contact.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the Laws, which regulate marriage as a matter of civic concern; free dissolution without grounds is not envisaged, though the Republic's guardians have no private marriage.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Plato argues that rule belongs to those who know the good, not to instruction by the ruled, and criticises democracy as rule by the unlearned.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the Republic and Laws, where the city regulates wealth and retirement of citizens collectively; private accumulation for individual ends runs against its aims.

land-use-tenure.rationale: In the Laws the land is divided into fixed allotments held by citizens on behalf of the state, which cannot be sold or accumulated; guardians in the Republic own no land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed directly; the Laws' mixed constitution includes magistrates who audit public finances, but a parliament in the modern sense is outside the thought.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the Laws' uniform civic education and religion, which unify the city on a common culture; no evidence of plural official languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The Laws restrict foreigners' property and settlement, keeping the allotments in citizens' hands as a condition of the city's stability.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from Plato's view that justice means each doing their natural task in a hierarchy, so equality of outcomes between groups is no test of justice.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Republic holds that luxury and the pursuit of unlimited wealth corrupt the city and cause war, and the Laws limit wealth to keep citizens virtuous.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the Republic's view of war as arising from luxury and as a last resort; arming foreign factions is not discussed.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the Laws' emphasis on a self-sufficient, self-governing city; intervention within a league of cities is not discussed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: the Republic holds that wealth corrupts rulers and bars its guardians from private riches.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the Laws' tight regulation of foreign contact to protect the city's education and character.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The Laws and Republic have the city regulate marriage and births to keep its numbers stable, so state action on population fits, though the aim differs.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the Laws, where land is allotted to citizens and kept within the city's households.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: justice means each citizen doing a fitting task and the city assigns them, though employer of last resort is a modern idea.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Republic treats democracy as rule by the unlearned and a degenerate regime, so spreading it is not a route to a good order.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Laws stresses citizens' obedience to law as a condition of the good city.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed beyond rules for war among Greeks; split between city self-containment and the rule of the wise.

industrial-unions.rationale: Anachronistic; the Republic assigns each person one craft but gives no view on unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: the Republic builds the city on reason and justice, which leave no place for such claims.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Republic abolishes private family for guardians but under strict state control, and the Laws regulates marriage by law, so marriage is a public institution, not a private one.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Republic has rulers censor stories and use a 'noble lie', so unrestricted public access to information is not endorsed.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the Laws' city placed away from the sea to keep it largely self-sufficient and limit trade.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: the Republic's order rests on a formal hierarchy of rulers, auxiliaries and producers and on education.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: the Laws makes the city's own law supreme and self-contained.

religious-nation.rationale: The Laws establishes state cults and punishes impiety, but the Republic's community rests on shared virtue and education.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the Republic, which traces war to luxury and expansion and sets a self-sufficient city, not tribute.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the Laws' self-sufficient city of fixed land allotments, which implies local use of local wealth.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Plato's guardians hold even homes and goods in common, so private personal possessions are not the rule for the ruling class.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not addressed; Plato's own guardian communism and his hostility to democracy leave adherents split on defeating communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from the Republic's state-run education and guardian system, which gives no role to private providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Laws punish impiety and treat civic religion as necessary for virtue, so religion is not an illusion to fade.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Plato's distrust of wealth-seeking, which corrupts the city, so capitalism is not a progressive force.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Republic admits women to the guardian class with equal education and ties this to abolishing the guardians' private households and property.

socialized-care.rationale: The Republic has the guardians' children raised communally by the state, removing childrearing from private families.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; Plato regulates poetry and education but never language purity, so this is a split call.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from Plato's view that law is supreme in the city and justice requires keeping commitments.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Guardians live communally, but the Republic puts power in philosopher-rulers, not self-governing communities, so this is split.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the Laws, where the lawgiver founds a colony and assigns allotments to bind the citizens to the city.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Laws' mixed constitution with limits on wealth and poverty, a middle course between extremes.

missingStatements.text: Art, poetry and stories should be censored if they harm citizens' moral character.
missingStatements.rationale: The Republic puts poetry and tales under state censorship and the Laws also regulates what citizens are taught, so that education serves virtue.

notes: The Republic and Laws differ: the Laws drops guardian communism and philosopher rule in favour of law and a mixed constitution. This profile follows the Republic for rule and the Laws where it describes the practical city.
